name: Washington

covered: Corporate officers (may elect out of State Fund)

workersCompensation.fundingModel: MONOPOLISTIC STATE FUND — Washington is one of four states where private workers' comp insurance is not allowed; all employers must insure through L&I State Fund or be certified self-insurers

benefitCategories.medical: All proper and necessary treatment; no fee schedule limits for most services
benefitCategories.timeLoss: 60-75% of wages (varies by marital/dependent status) up to 120% of state average; until claim closes or pension
benefitCategories.permanentPartialDisability: Category ratings or scheduled awards; lump sum or monthly based on impairment
benefitCategories.permanentTotalDisability: Pension at 60-75% of wages for life; cost-of-living adjustments
benefitCategories.deathBenefits: Pension to spouse; lump sum to children; burial $11,000+

workersCompensation.initialClaimForm: Report of Industrial Injury/Occupational Disease (filed by worker or employer)

appealLevels.name: Board of Industrial Insurance Appeals (BIIA)
appealLevels.deadline: 60 days from L&I order or 30 days from reconsideration

workersCompensation.enforcementPowers: L&I investigations; penalties for non-compliance; premium audits
workersCompensation.penalties: Penalties for late premium; benefits for retaliation against claimants; fraud prosecution

programs.name: Paid Family and Medical Leave
programs.eligibility: 820 hours worked in qualifying period; own serious health condition or family care
programs.benefitAmount: Up to 90% of wages (progressive formula); max $1,456/week (2024)
programs.duration: Up to 12 weeks medical; 12 weeks family; 16 weeks combined; 18 weeks pregnancy complications
programs.wcInteraction: Cannot receive PFML and workers' comp time-loss simultaneously

programs.name: Apple Health (Medicaid)
programs.eligibility: Low-income; Washington expanded Medicaid under ACA

statutes.name: Washington Law Against Discrimination (WLAD)
statutes.coverage: Employers with 8+ employees (1+ for some provisions)
statutes.protections: Disability discrimination; one of oldest and broadest state civil rights laws

statutes.name: Washington Family Leave Act
statutes.protections: 12 weeks unpaid leave; coordinates with PFML

civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Retaliation prohibited for opposing violations, filing complaints, or participating in proceedings

accommodationObligations.standard: Reasonable accommodation; interactive process; broader than ADA

delegatedBodies.authority: Workers' comp and workplace safety rules (WAC 296)

laborStandards.authority: Minimum Wage Act; Paid Sick Leave; wage claims

occupationalSafety.agency: L&I Division of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH)
occupationalSafety.authority: Washington OSHA; state plan state covering public and private

filingDeadlines.wcClaim: 1 year from injury (occupational disease: 2 years from knowledge)
filingDeadlines.pfmlClaim: Submit claim at least 30 days before leave when foreseeable

evidentiaryStandards.wc: Preponderance of evidence; objective findings required for many conditions

judicialReview.wc: L&I → BIIA → Superior Court → Court of Appeals → Supreme Court
judicialReview.wlad: WSHRC (optional) or direct Superior Court filing → appellate courts
judicialReview.directFiling: No requirement to exhaust WSHRC before filing civil lawsuit

specialConsiderations.monopolisticStateFund: Washington is one of 4 monopolistic state fund states (with Ohio, North Dakota, Wyoming). Private WC insurance not sold; employers use State Fund or self-insure.
specialConsiderations.pfmlProgram: Washington's PFML (2020) is one of the most generous state programs; combines with FMLA for comprehensive leave
specialConsiderations.doshCoverage: State OSHA plan covers both public and private sectors with strong enforcement
specialConsiderations.strongProtections: Washington is considered one of the most worker-protective states for both WC and civil rights
